title: GPU nodepool upgrade-safety Terraform module for Private VPC (ASG + Karpenter interoperability)
creator: Evan Huang
description: Build a reusable Terraform module to provision GPU node groups in customer Private VPCs that supports both ASG-backed nodepools and Karpenter-managed capacity, with integrated health checks and safe upgrade orchestration. The goal is to provide a single module teams can instantiate to get: mixed-instance GPU pools, spot + on-demand fallback, controlled rolling upgrades with pre-drain validation, GPU driver compatibility checks, and observability hooks for SLOs. This will replace ad-hoc in-repo provisioning patterns and reduce upgrade-related incidents during driver or kernel rollouts.
background: Customers running Private deployments have experienced pod evictions and ML job failures during GPU driver upgrades and AMI rebuilds. Existing Terraform snippets are inconsistent across accounts. We need a hardened module that codifies best practices (cordon/drain grace periods, drain-safety probes, warm pool pre-provisioning) and works for both ASG-based nodepools and Karpenter spot/ondemand mixes.
proposal: Create tf module 'redwood_tf_gpu_nodepool' with features: 1) 'mode' param: 'asg' or 'karpenter' controlling resources created and IAM roles. 2) Mixed instance types list + GPU type constraints. 3) Prewarm node capacity option (warm_pool or preprovision_count). 4) Upgrade strategy: canary batch size, cordon+drain with custom node-health-check webhook, automated retry/backoff. 5) Driver lifecycle hook: user-data or SSM run-command that validates NVIDIA driver, DCGM exporter, and nvidia-device-plugin before marking node healthy. 6) Terraform outputs and tags for observability (provision_time, last_upgrade_commit). 7) Integration test suite using Terratest + a smoke cluster in staging VPC.
technical_design: Module inputs: vpc_id, subnet_ids, instance_profile_arn, ami_map, gpu_specs (list), node_labels, taints, mode, spot_fallback_policy, prewarm_count, drain_timeout_seconds, health_probe_endpoint. Resources vary by mode: ASG: launch template, autoscaling group, lifecycle hooks, warm pool optionally; Karpenter: provisioner CRD manifest with nodeSelector and constraints pushed via Terraform kubernetes provider. Add an AWS SSM document and IAM role to run post-boot validation. Health check flow: after node boot -> run driver/daemonset self-checks -> write to a 'node-healthy' tag via AWS SDK or annotate via Kubernetes API. Terraform waits for the healthy signal during rolling upgrades using null_resource+local-exec polling (with max timeout). For safety, upgrades default to conservative batch sizes and require manual approval if GPU feature changing. The module emits Prometheus labels and CloudWatch metrics hooks, and exposes a 'safe_to_upgrade' data source that other automation can query.
acceptance_criteria:
- Module can be instantiated in staging VPC in both 'asg' and 'karpenter' modes.
- Controlled upgrade: trigger ami bump; system performs canary of at least 1 node and only proceeds when canary reports healthy for 10 minutes.
- No more than 1% job failure rate across test ML jobs during upgrade (baseline).
- Terratest suite passes end-to-end including driver validation and pod scheduling.
- Documentation and example usage for private deployment and for enabling warm pool preprovisioning.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge module into infra-modules repo on feature branch. 2) Deploy to staging VPC using example overlay. 3) Run terratest and smoke ML jobs (bert microbenchmark). 4) Iterate on failures, add metrics dashboards. 5) Offer to two pilot customers for Private deployment (controlled rollout). 6) After pilot validation, cut a release tag and notify platform teams to adopt.
testing_plan:
- Unit: Terraform validate + fmt + static checks.
- Integration: Terratest (Go) that provisions in a fresh staging namespace and runs: driver_install_check, DCGM export, pod placement on GPU, node cordon/drain simulation.
- Chaos tests: simulate spot interruption (if mode==karpenter) and ensure fallback to on-demand or other instance types works.
- Upgrade tests: automated ami/driver upgrades with canary and rollback verification.
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: RFC drafted and shared with infra-owner channel (initial approach: single module supporting both provisioning modes).

2026-02-24: Design review with Platform and Runtime teams. Decided to use SSM-based post-boot validation rather than waiting on DaemonSet only, for faster certificate-less verification in Private VPCs.
2026-03-02: PoC terraform submodule created that provisions ASG with warm_pool and lifecycle hook. Canary logic implemented in a 'upgrade' script used by CI.

2026-03-09: Discovered edge case: Karpenter provisioner will not honor warm_pool semantics; we will instead use a prewarm_count approach and create dummy pods to force node allocation. Added to design doc.
2026-03-12: First terratest run in staging succeeded for ASG mode. Karpenter mode tests failing due to IAM permissions for provisioner controller; follow-up assigned.
open_questions:
- Should the module manage AMI bake pipelines or just accept AMI IDs? (current proposal: accept AMI IDs and provide optional helper for AMI metadata).
- Do we want to favor node tagging vs Kubernetes annotation for 'node-healthy' signalling in private clusters where cross-account roles are limited?
- What should be the default prewarm_count for small-to-medium customers to balance cost vs rollout safety?
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Long terraform apply times during rolling upgrades could block automation. Mitigation: use asynchronous apply patterns and break upgrades into smaller plans.
- Risk: Spot eviction causing capacity loss during upgrade. Mitigation: conservative canary size + spot diversification + on-demand fallback policy.
- Risk: Driver mismatch causing node flapping. Mitigation: post-boot driver validation and automatic cordon if validation fails.
next_steps: 1) Finish Karpenter IAM adjustments (assigned to Miguel Ortega). 2) Harden terratest to cover spot interruption path. 3) Add sample overlays and docs for customers to opt into warm_pool/prewarm_count. 4) Schedule pilot rollout with Platform SRE (target 2026-03-29).
notes: This module is focused on Private VPC deployments where we cannot rely on managed EKS nodegroup semantics. Emphasize observability and explicit health signalling to avoid surprise evictions during upgrades. The implementation must be easy to consume for solution engineers supporting on-prem customers.
